key_insight: Strong diagnostic performance did not ensure reliable downstream cancer care, with dominant LLM failure modes shifting across care phases.
clinical_relevance: The findings support phase-specific evaluation and safeguards rather than relying on diagnostic accuracy alone to assess clinical reliability.
method: Developed NPC-RubricBench from longitudinal nasopharyngeal carcinoma records across six care phases.
Scored 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs using patient-specific criteria restricted to decision-time evidence.
Compared failure patterns across phases and tested broad versus checklist-like prompts.
evidence_signal: The benchmark included 405 patients from two cancer centers, 941 patient-phase units, and 17,688 atomic criteria across five evaluation dimensions.
watch_item: More detailed prompts improved Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence, highlighting a trade-off in prompt design.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
